question: do the two hosts actually activate the same Windows ML runtime?
answer: At the API layer yes: the official `windowsml` 2.5.96 wheel ships its own Microsoft.Windows.AI.MachineLearning.dll and that binary is byte-identical on both hosts. The catalog decision is therefore made by the same code from different system inputs.
loaded_vs_os_binary_note: The wheel DLL (loaded by the Python probe) is NOT the same file as the OS WindowsWorkload.WinMLShared.7.0 DLL. Both are Microsoft-signed; only the wheel DLL contains the AMDGPU/WebGPU catalogue entries, so the wheel is the authoritative catalogue source for this API surface.

native_controls.independent_process: each probe ran in its own interpreter process

excluded: same-SDK/different-runtime at the API layer (binary identical)
Python binding artifact (both the wheel flat-C API and the WinAppSDK projection return 0 in this same session; the DLL is what the OS sees)
